  16 
  17 \section{Two-screen scintillation formalism and screen-distance constraints}
  18 \label{app:twoscreen}
  19 % AASTeX resets the equation counter in each appendix section, while hyperref's
  20 % default anchor uses only that counter. Include the section in the anchor so
  21 % these equations do not reuse destinations from earlier appendix sections.
  22 \renewcommand{\theHequation}{\thesection.\arabic{equation}}
  23 
  24 This appendix collects the diffractive-scintillation estimator and the
  25 two-screen geometric framework that Section~\ref{sec:results-scintillation}
  26 and the screen attribution of Section~\ref{sec:disc-screen-attribution} draw
  27 on. It defines quantities and relations only; the per-sightline application
  28 is made in the main text from the provisional fit products, and
  29 robust interpretation remains conditional on independent verification of the
  30 scintillation and scattering strands. Throughout, the fitted decorrelation
  31 bandwidth written $\gamma$ in Section~\ref{sec:results-scintillation} is
  32 denoted $\nu_{s}$ here ($\gamma\equiv\Delta\nu_{d}\equiv\nu_{s}$, the
  33 Lorentzian half-width at half-maximum), reserving $\gamma$ for that section's
  34 usage.
  35 
  36 \subsection{ACF-based diffractive-scintillation estimator}
  37 \label{app:acf}
  38 
  39 For each burst the on-pulse spectrum $I(\nu)$ is formed by averaging the
  40 dynamic spectrum over the on-pulse samples, with the noise level estimated
  41 from an off-pulse region. The one-dimensional frequency autocorrelation
  42 function (ACF) of the mean-subtracted spectrum is
  43 %
  44 \begin{equation}
  45 \mathrm{ACF}(\delta\nu)
  46   = \frac{\big\langle\, \Delta I(\nu)\,\Delta I(\nu+\delta\nu)\,\big\rangle_\nu}
  47          {\big\langle I(\nu)\big\rangle_\nu^2},
  48 \qquad
  49 \Delta I(\nu) \equiv I(\nu) - \big\langle I(\nu)\big\rangle_\nu,
  50 \label{eq:acf}
  51 \end{equation}
  52 %
  53 where $\langle\cdot\rangle_\nu$ averages over frequency channels. This
  54 normalization is by the squared mean intensity, rather than by the spectral
  55 variance, so that the noise-corrected zero-lag amplitude is the squared
  56 modulation index. The
  57 zero-lag point ($\delta\nu=0$) is excluded from all fits: radiometer noise is
  58 uncorrelated between channels and contributes a delta-function spike at
  59 $\delta\nu=0$ that biases the peak upward by the noise variance. The
  60 scintillation modulation index $m\equiv\sigma_I/\langle I\rangle$ is recovered
  61 as the noise-corrected zero-lag amplitude, i.e.\ the fitted model extrapolated
  62 to $\delta\nu\to0$,
  63 %
  64 \begin{equation}
  65 \mathrm{ACF}(0^{+}) = m^{2}.
  66 \label{eq:m2}
  67 \end{equation}
  68 %
  69 A point source in the strong-scattering regime gives $m=1$; a source whose
  70 apparent angular size partially resolves the scattering disk gives $m<1$
  71 (partial quenching), the property exploited in Appendix~\ref{app:distance}.
  72 Each diffractive component is modeled with the Lorentzian derived by
  73 \citet{Gwinn1998} for a single thin screen,
  74 %
  75 \begin{equation}
  76 \mathrm{ACF}(\delta\nu)
  77   = \frac{m^{2}}{1 + (\delta\nu/\nu_{s})^{2}},
  78 \label{eq:lorentzian}
  79 \end{equation}
  80 %
  81 with $\nu_{s}$ the decorrelation bandwidth (the $\gamma$ of
  82 Section~\ref{sec:results-scintillation}). The decorrelation bandwidth and the
  83 pulse-broadening time $\tau_{s}$ from the same screen are conjugate through
  84 the Fourier uncertainty relation
  85 %
  86 \begin{equation}
  87 2\pi\,\nu_{s}\,\tau_{s} = C_{1},
  88 \label{eq:c1}
  89 \end{equation}
  90 %
  91 with $C_{1}$ a geometry- and spectrum-dependent constant of order unity that
  92 ranges over $0.5$--$2$ across plausible screen-geometry and turbulence-spectrum
  93 combinations \citep{LambertRickett1999,Pradeep2025}. We adopt $C_{1}=1$ as the
  94 fiducial thin-screen value and propagate the full $0.5$--$2$ range as a
  95 systematic on any $\tau_{s}\leftrightarrow\nu_{s}$ conversion.
  96 
  97 \paragraph{Finite-sample statistics.}
  98 Across an observing band $B$ the number of independent scintles is
  99 $N_{\rm scint}\simeq\eta\,B/\nu_{s}$ with a filling factor $\eta=\mathcal{O}(1)$
 100 for scintle overlap. The finite scintle count sets an irreducible
 101 ``self-noise'' floor on the estimator, with fractional uncertainties
 102 %
 103 \begin{equation}
 104 \frac{\sigma_{\nu_{s}}}{\nu_{s}} \sim \frac{1}{\sqrt{N_{\rm scint}}},
 105 \qquad
 106 \frac{\sigma_{m}}{m} \sim \frac{1}{\sqrt{N_{\rm scint}}},
 107 \label{eq:selfnoise}
 108 \end{equation}
 109 %
 110 dominant when $\nu_{s}$ is a sizeable fraction of $B$ (few scintles across the
 111 band); it is added in quadrature with the radiometer-noise contribution when
 112 quoting uncertainties on $\nu_{s}$ and $m$.
 113 
 114 \subsection{Two-screen geometry}
 115 \label{app:geometry}
 116 
 117 Place the observer at $O$ and the source at angular-diameter distance $D$, with
 118 a near (Milky Way) screen at distance $d_{\rm MW}$ from $O$ and a far
 119 (host-galaxy) screen at $d_{h}$, $d_{\rm MW}<d_{h}<D$. A thin screen at
 120 distance $d$ imposes a scattering time
 121 %
 122 \begin{equation}
 123 \tau = \frac{\theta_{\rm scat}^{2}\,d_{\rm eff}}{2c},
 124 \qquad
 125 d_{\rm eff} = \frac{d\,(D-d)}{D},
 126 \label{eq:tau}
 127 \end{equation}
 128 %
 129 so $\theta_{\rm scat}=\sqrt{2c\tau/d_{\rm eff}}$ and the diffractive
 130 field-coherence scale is $s_{d}=\lambda/(2\pi\theta_{\rm scat})$; cosmological
 131 $(1+z)$ factors enter the far-screen terms and are carried explicitly in
 132 Eq.~(\ref{eq:distance}).
 133 
 134 \paragraph{Apparent size of the host image.}
 135 The quantity governing whether one screen resolves the other is the angular
 136 size of the host scattering disk projected to the near screen. A
 137 first-principles ray-trace (point source at $D$, thin deflector at $d_{h}$,
 138 observing plane at $d_{\rm MW}$) gives
 139 %
 140 \begin{equation}
 141 \theta_{\rm img}
 142   = \theta_{{\rm scat},h}\,\frac{D-d_{h}}{D-d_{\rm MW}} ,
 143 \label{eq:thimg}
 144 \end{equation}
 145 %
 146 which in the limit $d_{\rm MW}\to0$ reduces to the observed image size
 147 $\theta_{h}\simeq\theta_{{\rm scat},h}(D-d_{h})/D=(2c\tau_{h}\,d_{ls,h})^{1/2}/D$,
 148 with $d_{ls,h}=D-d_{h}$ \citep{Masui2015}. (The lever-arm denominator is
 149 $D-d_{\rm MW}$, the far-screen-to-near-screen path measured from the source
 150 side; the screen--screen separation $d_{h}-d_{\rm MW}$ would fail this
 151 observer limit.)
 152 
 153 \paragraph{Resolution power.}
 154 The near screen acts as an interferometer of effective aperture $L_{\rm MW}$
 155 and angular resolution $\theta_{\rm res}=\lambda/L_{\rm MW}$.
 156 \citet{Pradeep2025} parameterize the degree of resolution by the resolution
 157 power
 158 %
 159 \begin{equation}
 160 \mathrm{RP} \equiv \frac{\Theta_{\rm size}}{\theta_{\rm res}}
 161   = \frac{L_{\rm MW}\,L_{\rm host}}{\lambda\,D_{\rm MW,host}},
 162 \label{eq:rp}
 163 \end{equation}
 164 %
 165 where $L_{\rm MW},L_{\rm host}$ are the transverse scattering-disk sizes and
 166 $D_{\rm MW,host}$ the angular-diameter distance between the screens.
 167 $\mathrm{RP}\ll1$: screens do not resolve each other (both scintillation
 168 scales visible); $\mathrm{RP}\simeq1$: marginal resolution; $\mathrm{RP}\gg1$:
 169 the near screen resolves the far screen and the associated broad-scale
 170 scintillation is quenched.
 171 
 172 \subsection{Modulation-index parameterization for two screens}
 173 \label{app:modindex}
 174 
 175 With two screens the total spectral ACF is not the sum of the two Lorentzians:
 176 \citet{Pradeep2025} show it carries an additional product term,
 177 %
 178 \begin{equation}
 179 \mathrm{ACF}_{\rm tot}(\delta\nu)
 180   = \underbrace{m_{\rm MW}^{2}\,\rho_{\rm MW}(\delta\nu)
 181   + m_{h}^{2}\,\rho_{h}(\delta\nu)}_{\text{sum of screens}}
 182   + \underbrace{m_{\rm MW}^{2}\,m_{h}^{2}\,
 183       \rho_{\rm MW}(\delta\nu)\,\rho_{h}(\delta\nu)}_{\text{product term}},
 184 \label{eq:acf2}
 185 \end{equation}
 186 %
 187 with $\rho_{s}(\delta\nu)=[1+(\delta\nu/\nu_{s,s})^{2}]^{-1}$. In the
 188 unresolved regime with both screens fully modulated
 189 ($m_{\rm MW}=m_{h}=1$), the noise-free zero-lag value is
 190 $\mathrm{ACF}_{\rm tot}(0^{+})=3$, so the combined modulation index rises to
 191 %
 192 \begin{equation}
 193 m_{\rm tot} = \sqrt{3}\qquad(\text{unresolved, fully modulated}).
 194 \label{eq:sqrt3}
 195 \end{equation}
 196 %
 197 As the near screen begins to resolve the far screen, the broad-scale component
 198 is progressively (not abruptly) quenched: $m_{\rm MW}$ declines toward zero
 199 with increasing RP, the product term collapses, and $m_{\rm tot}$ falls back
 200 toward the single-screen value. The measured
 201 $\{m_{\rm MW},m_{h},\nu_{s,\rm MW},\nu_{s,h}\}$ therefore diagnose the
 202 resolution regime directly.
 203 
 204 \subsection{Host-screen distance constraint}
 205 \label{app:distance}
 206 
 207 The physical argument \citep{Masui2015,CordesChatterjee2019} is that the near
 208 (MW) screen imprints scintillation only if the host image it views is
 209 unresolved, $\theta_{\rm img}\lesssim\theta_{\rm res,MW}$ (equivalently
 210 $\mathrm{RP}\lesssim1$). Observing MW scintillation therefore bounds the host
 211 scattering angle from above and, since $\theta_{{\rm scat},h}$ is fixed by the
 212 measured host $\tau_{h}$ through Eq.~(\ref{eq:tau}), bounds the product of
 213 screen distances. In the redshift-consistent form of \citet{Pradeep2025},
 214 %
 215 \begin{equation}
 216 D_{h,\rm FRB}\,D_{\rm MW}
 217   \;\lesssim\;
 218   \frac{(1+z_{\rm FRB})\,D_{\rm FRB}^{2}}{8\pi\,\nu^{2}}\,
 219   \frac{\nu_{s,\rm MW}}{m_{\rm MW}\,\tau_{s,h}},
 220 \label{eq:distance}
 221 \end{equation}
 222 %
 223 where $D_{h,\rm FRB}$ is the source--host-screen distance, $D_{\rm MW}$ the
 224 observer--MW-screen distance, $\nu$ the observing frequency, $\nu_{s,\rm MW}$
 225 the MW decorrelation bandwidth, $m_{\rm MW}$ the MW modulation index, and
 226 $\tau_{s,h}$ the host scattering time. With $D_{\rm FRB}$ and $z_{\rm FRB}$
 227 fixed by the host redshift and $D_{\rm MW}$ estimated from a Galactic
 228 electron-density model \citep{CordesLazio2002}, this is an upper limit on
 229 $D_{h,\rm FRB}$.
 230 
 231 The modulation-index factor corrects the resolution-induced broadening of the
 232 measured MW scintillation bandwidth, but it does not turn
 233 Eq.~(\ref{eq:distance}) into an equality. In particular, reduced but detected
 234 MW modulation ($0<m_{\rm MW}<1$) is evidence for partial resolution, not proof
 235 that the geometric threshold is exactly saturated. The transition is gradual,
 236 and stochastic screen realizations produce appreciable scatter at fixed
 237 resolution power \citep{Pradeep2025}. We therefore retain
 238 Eq.~(\ref{eq:distance}) as an upper limit for all resolution regimes in which
 239 the MW component remains measurable. A future calibrated likelihood linking
 240 $\{m_{\rm MW},\nu_{s,\rm MW}\}$ to RP could support posterior inference on
 241 $D_{h,\rm FRB}$, but such an inference would be model-dependent and would not
 242 be a point-distance measurement obtained by saturating this inequality.
 243 
 244 \paragraph{Caveats.} Equation~(\ref{eq:distance}) assumes both screens are
 245 two-dimensional (isotropic) in the plane of the sky; for
 246 one-dimensional (elongated) screens the relative position angle enters and the
 247 scalar relation breaks down \citep{Pradeep2025}. Because the broad-scale
 248 quenching is gradual, ``marginal resolution'' is a regime rather than a
 249 knife-edge; any later posterior use of the relation must include the calibrated
 250 RP dependence and realization scatter. Consistency check:
 251 representative sample values give $L_{x}L_{g}\lesssim\text{few}\
 252 \mathrm{kpc}^{2}$, in line with the CRAFT two-screen constraints of
 253 \citet{Sammons2023}.

# Free-alpha diagnostic evidence packet

Read-only capture from h17 on 2026-07-22. It preserves three diagnostic
families: six scintillation-gain products, seven component-leakage products,
and five tail-plus-component products. Ten component-grid products and all six
scintillation products have successful, empty-error Slurm logs. Two additional
pilot products have no recovered launch logs. It also preserves current driver,
job-script, fitter-provenance, and campaign-input bytes.

The copied evidence totals about 260 KiB. `SHA256SUMS` binds all 60 copied
artifact. `manifest.json` records the host, environment, remote paths, code
commits, and important limitations: the driver and fitter provenance were
untracked in their h17 worktree, so no repository commit proves they are the
exact runtime bytes. The campaign-input records postdate the injections by one
day. Only physical injection parameters needed to check the landed bias
arithmetic are embedded; sampler and runtime settings remain incomplete.
Observed environment versions may have drifted since the July 18 runs.

Verify from a clean checkout with Python 3.10 or newer; only the standard
library is required:

```bash
python3 docs/rse/specs/research/evidence/free-alpha-diagnostic-2026-07-22/verify_packet.py
```

The verifier checks hashes and the exact filesystem roster, input diagnostic status,
the analytic within-channel modulation suppression, posterior ordering,
bias arithmetic, agreement between scheduled products and logs, successful
return codes, empty error logs, and the reported bounds. `grid_roster.json`
records every recovered multi-component product and distinguishes the two
unlogged pilots.

Recovered bounds are exact over these rosters: the minimum component-only bias
is `-0.43040582429955254` among seven products; the minimum combined-tail-and-
component bias is `-0.8561575297363464` among five. These grids did not reproduce
the approximately `-1.6` anomaly. They do not universally exclude either
mechanism outside the recovered tested envelope.

Independent parsing found one metadata-only defect. The driver constructs an
inclusive 400--800 MHz frequency grid, so the spacing used in the effective
modulation calculation is 400 MHz divided by `nchan - 1`. The JSON field
`chan_width_mhz_target` records the nominal 400 MHz divided by `nchan` value.
The stored effective modulation values agree with the actual grid spacing, so
the injection and leakage bounds are unaffected. Do not reuse the nominal JSON
field as the exact simulated channel spacing.
